observations: Photo 0 shows a dual-head embroidery machine with two needle bars, each labeled 'Yinghe' in blue script.
The machine has a control panel with a screen on the right side, partially wrapped in plastic.
There are embroidery hoops, spools of thread, and some tools on the table.
Photo 1 shows the same machine from a slightly different angle, with more tools and parts visible, including a yellow box labeled in Chinese characters.
The machine appears to be in a workshop or storage area, not a retail setting.
The seller claims it is 'brand new' and 'Yinghe 2 head embroidery'.

claims.evidence: No signs of use are visible, but no proof of original packaging, serial number, or factory seal. The machine appears assembled and possibly used, with tools and parts scattered around.
The brand name 'Yinghe' is clearly visible on both needle bars in photo 0 and photo 1. The machine has two heads, matching the description.

risks.risk: machine may not be functional or may have been used
risks.proof: A video showing the machine powering on, running a test stitch, and the control panel responding to inputs.
A complete inventory shot showing all included components, manuals, and original packaging.
A close-up of the serial number plate or factory label, and a photo of the original box with brand and model details.

proof_requests: Video of the machine powering on and running a test embroidery pattern.
Photo of the serial number plate or factory label.
Photo of the original packaging and all included accessories.
Photo of the control panel screen showing the machine's software interface.
response.reason: The brand and type are confirmed, but the 'brand new' claim is unverified. The machine's functionality, completeness, and authenticity cannot be confirmed from the photos alone. Proof is needed to determine if it is truly new and working.
